newsitem.title: USA: BPA lowers Friday peak, firm power $1.25/MWh.
newsitem.headline: BPA lowers Friday peak, firm power $1.25/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) lowered firm peak power prices for Friday by $1.25 per megawatt hour (MWh) and offered non-firm power during shoulder hours at $9.00 a MWh, BPA said Thursday.
BPA still offered 300 megawatts of firm peak power, but lowered prices to $12.25 per megawatt hour (MWh) for Northwest sales and $13.25 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
BPA also continued to offer power at $7.00 per MWh during hours ending 0100-0600 and 2300-2400 PST to buyers willing to displace thermal generation with hydropower.
Non-firm power during off-peak and shoulder hours on Friday (0100-0600, 1100-1700 and 2100-2400 PST) was offered at $9.00 per MWh for all deliveries.
Prices for firm power during off-peak hours on Friday were unchanged at $9.00 per MWh.
